title: [Regression 6.2.0] Rootless container fails to start with NVIDIA CDI devices: crun: mount_setattr: Operation not permitted
body:
### Issue Description

### Description
After upgrading `podman` from `6.1.4` to `6.2.0-1` (along with `containers-common 0.70.0-2`), rootless containers using NVIDIA CDI (`--device ://nvidia.com`, e.g., via Distrobox / davincibox) fail to start with a `mount_setattr` permission error from `crun`.

Downgrading `podman` back to `6.1.4-1.1` and `containers-common` to `0.69.2-1` immediately resolves the issue.

### Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Use a rootless Podman setup on Arch Linux / CachyOS with NVIDIA proprietary drivers (`620.70.06`) and `nvidia-container-toolkit` generating `/var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml`.
2. Upgrade `podman` to `6.2.0-1`.
3. Try to start an existing rootless container with NVIDIA CDI devices attached (`distrobox enter davincibox`).

### Describe the results you received
The container fails to start with:
```text
Error: unable to start container "...": crun: mount_setattr `/run/nvidia-persistenced/socket`: Operation not permitted: OCI permission denied
```
Even when `nvidia-persistenced` is stopped and regenerated without the socket, `crun` fails on the next bind-mounted host binary in the CDI spec:
```text
Error: unable to start container "...": crun: mount_setattr `/usr/bin/nvidia-cuda-mps-control`: Operation not permitted: OCI permission denied
```

### Describe the results you expected
The rootless container should start normally and mount the NVIDIA CDI devices and libraries as it did in Podman `6.1.4`.

### Additional environment details
- **OS:** CachyOS (Arch Linux x86_64)
- **Kernel:** `7.3.3-1-cachyos`
- **Podman version (broken):** `6.2.0-1` (`containers-common 1:0.70.0-2`)
- **Podman version (working):** `6.1.4-1.1` (`containers-common 1:0.69.2-1`)
- **OCI Runtime:** `crun 1.30.1-1.1`
- **NVIDIA Driver / CDI spec:** `620.70.06` (`cdiVersion: 0.7.0`)

comments.body:
This looks like the CDI v1.1.0 -> v1.1.1 bump in 6.2.0 (#29719). CDI now auto-adds `idmap`/`ridmap` to bind mounts whenever a user namespace is present ([container-device-interface#288](https://github.com/cncf-tags/container-device-interface/pull/288)). Rootless always has a `userns`, so NVIDIA CDI mounts hit `mount_setattr` -> `EPERM` (idmapped mounts aren’t available rootless).

Typical NVIDIA CDI mounts don’t need `idmap` (6.1.4 worked without it). So I would strip those options in Podman when rootless for all  CDIs. I am not sure if we should strip that always.  

cc @elezar @podman-container-tools/podman-maintainers
is there any particular reason to use `idmap/ridmap` at all in this case?  Is it to give access to non-root?

> Rootless always has a userns, so NVIDIA CDI mounts hit mount_setattr -> EPERM (idmapped mounts aren’t available rootless).

That not really true though. no? Like yes we run within a userns but that is just the namespace crun will run in, we do not tell crun to create a new userns with custom mappings by default unless a user requests that.

IMO its not our task to strip out broken CDI options from the spec again, we have to trust CDI to generate something functional. I don't think adding such options unconditionally in CDI is the right thing to do.
idmap mounts are only supported as real root on the host, no? Like even in a nested userns as uid you can use them so that means cdi is now unusable in nested cotnainers?

They would work if the parent container has capabilities and no user namespace.  idmapped mounts (unless the user owns the source mount) are allowed only in the initial user namespace.

I agree though that they should not be used by default in the CDI
The following was merged for this https://github.com/cncf-tags/container-device-interface/pull/371 on the CDI side. We will include it in the next patch release.

My apologies. Then I didn't fully grok the problem. Let me spend a bit more time on it.

As a follow-up question: How would CDI detect whether "idmapped mounts are available"?

@giuseppe can likely elaborate more but as basic thing it must be part of the initial user namespace
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/blob/83df295d5a2e3a1562e9906cce8c86cef7fb6eb6/storage/pkg/unshare/unshare_linux.go#L397-L409

But then there are also other concerns, the oci runtime must support this. The linux kernel version must support it, while idmapped mount support is now in the kernel for a while AFAIK it still depends on support of the backing fs, i.e. support for idmapped overlay mounts were just added very recently I think.

Overall I do not think sure that such a generic lib like the cdi code should make that choice in any case. Maybe it should have some API that lets the caller control this, then we can run our normal checks in podman and just pass a bool or similar to cdi calls. For real root we could turn it on but leave it off as rootless then

> Overall I do not think sure that such a generic lib like the cdi code should make that choice in any case. Maybe it should have some API that lets the caller control this, then we can run our normal checks in podman and just pass a bool or similar to cdi calls. For real root we could turn it on but leave it off as rootless then

We could make the behaviour opt-out when consitructing the `Cache` that applies the modifications to the CDI spec. The default would be the behaviour that we have, and Podman would opt-out in the rootless case. The alternative would be for k8s to opt-in in the cases for which it was initially introduced. @klihub would have to weigh in on the feasibility of that.

> As a follow-up question: How would CDI detect whether "idmapped mounts are available"?

> Overall I do not think sure that such a generic lib like the cdi code should make that choice in any case. Maybe it should have some API that lets the caller control this

@Luap99 @elezar So is it so that basically CDI would need to know 2 things to make the right decision: 1) if idmapped mounts are available at all on the host, and 2) if for this particular device injection, mounts should be injected idmapped (if it is available) ? And if it is so, is there enough information present in the OCI Spec we're injecting into, to decide the latter one ?

Or would a global option be enough for podman to turn idmapped mounts off altogether ? If it is enough then a cache-level opt-out or a global setting API would work. But if it is more complex, if it can vary injection by injection on the same host then this would not be enough.

it is more complicated than that, not every file system supports idmapped mounts (and some allow to be mapped inside a user namespace if the user namespace owns that mount).

I'd not introduce different behaviors unless it is strictly necessary, what was the problem that required using idmapped mounts?
This was the problem we added it for: https://github.com/cncf-tags/container-device-interface/issues/287

could this be solved by just changing the mode to 755?

I am asking because idmapped mounts won't work with rootless anyway, so it will break once there is a user namespace configured for rootless users, even if you allow access to the rootless user itself

> could this be solved by just changing the mode to 755?
 
> I am asking because idmapped mounts won't work with rootless anyway, so it will break once there is a user namespace configured for rootless users, even if you allow access to the rootless user itself

Do you mean changing the permissions of the bind-mounted directory on the host to 755 ? I don't know if that would be enough/work in all the cases. And I'm not sure if it would be acceptable for CDI to change permissions of the source directory.

Yes, and that will work in any case. No CDI should not change the mode autonomously as there might be good reasons for its original mode but could perhaps detect and print a warning so that whoever owns the directory can fix it.

I guess the question is who should decide what and how the it gets mounted?

Generally it is supposed to be the CDI config, right? Like you can pass mount options there already, no? So in theory one could just as well say set `idmap` as mount option in the CDI config file.
I am not sure if idmap acts as NOP when run without a userns, I would guess so? At least if I run without a container userns I can pass the option on rootless podman without issues.

But then that would just shift the problem from CDI go code instead into all the configs which want to work like that in a userns pod. So if a vendor would ship the cdi config with that option in it would still blow up for rootless podman with a custom userns mapping then like it got reported here.
However it would mean there is a text config a user/administrator could overwrite on the host to drop idmap from it to at least have something working. Seems better than the current hard coded version in the code to me.

CDI certainly should not mess with the permission of the passed in mounts. That is up to the system admin to decide.
